newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Orange, CAIB enter race for Austrian GSM licence.
newsitem.headline: Orange, CAIB enter race for Austrian GSM licence.

text.p: Britain's Orange Plc and Creditanstalt bank opened up the race for Austria's third mobile telephone licence on Wednesday when they submitted a joint bid minutes ahead of a government deadline.

"I can confirm that Creditanstalt Investment Bank and Orange have lodged a bid. Creditanstalt Investment Bank will have a 51 percent stake," a Creditanstalt spokesman told Reuters. He declined to give further details.
The newcomers are up against the long standing Connect Austria consortium, made up of industrial firm Radex-Heraklith, Germany's Viag, unlisted Constantia Privatbank and bank GiroCredit of Austria.
That group submitted its bid at the start of June.
"The Science and Transport Ministry has received two bids -- one on June 2 and the second this afternoon just before the 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) cut-off," a ministry spokesman confirmed.

He forecast a decision on the potentially lucrative GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) licence in mid-August. Investment house Deloitte & Touche will advise the government during a four-week evaluation period.
"Then we will open the auction for the licence fee," the spokesman said, referring to a process that will allow bidders to up their offers.

He said the government was unconcerned by threatened legal action by the Connect Austria consortium. The group alleges it was put at a disadvantage by a government decision to extend the bid deadline by one month.
"Both bids landed after the deadline extension was announced (at the end of May)," the spokesman said.

In December 1995, Austria's second mobile licence went for four billion schillings to max.mobil -- a consortium comprising Germany's DeTeMobil, the Austrian unit of Siemens and several banking partners.
Austrian media have speculated that the government will have difficulty raising more than 1.5 billion schillings from the third auction because of high setting up costs.

The nation's mobile phone network is almost entirely dominated by Mobilkom Austria, a unit of state postal and telecoms monopoly PTA. The market is due for liberalisation in 1998, one year ahead of PTA's planned privatisation.
Mobilkom is estimated to have some 650,000 mobile phone customers in Austria, a country of eight million, with about 400,000 of them in the GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) segment.
Max.mobil's customer base is believed to be a mere 25,000.
Orange Plc runs a digital network in Britain where it has 980,000 customers.
The new Austrian network will operate on 1800 MegaHertz. The existing second mobile phone network is on a 900 MegaHertz frequency.
